items.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Imagine playing opposite Art Tatum, and you’re playing with Bird, for four weeks.

ctx.x: Then sometimes Kenny Dorham was with us. I’ll never the forget the summer of – I guess it was June or July of 1950, which would have been the following year. We go into Café Society in the Village for four weeks, which was a long gig in New York,

opposite Art Tatum. Imagine playing opposite Art Tatum, and you’re playing with Bird, for four weeks. Opening night you can’t get in the place, and Billie Holiday comes up and sings with us. Can you imagine all that? We’re wearing ties and suits. I don’t even know if they had it air conditioned in the club in those days. But it was such a beautiful period. That was a beautiful time. Jesus. I couldn’t wait to go to work at night. The feeling. Lovely. I’m glad I did the period when I did, even came along, because…
Let’s talk about that first car you got – you’re so proud of in that picture. You’re talking about cars.
